MSW snapshot handler always returns the seed rev-B snapshot regardless of the :rev path param, so in dev, after issuing a new version, openSign computes nextStep from a stale snapshot (dev-only fidelity gap; real backend keys on rev).

Frontend gates everywhere consume the singular `role` from auth state (menu visibility, self-review check, sign-role mismatch); verification was grep-only — if the token ever carries multiple roles, these gates diverge from backend checks that use `actor.roles`.

findings.title: Mid-flight matrix rebind defeats APPROVAL_SELF_REVIEW_FORBIDDEN (CWE-863)
findings.suggested_fix: Freeze the approval chain at submit the same way deliverable versions do: store the normalized steps (matrix_id + parsed steps) in a JSON column on the record at submit-approval and have `_next_approval_role` read that snapshot instead of calling `resolve_project_matrix` live (mirroring the snapshot-first pattern in deliverable_service.py:1105-1130). As a complementary belt, re-assert the self-review rule at each approval step: reject with 403 APPROVAL_SELF_REVIEW_FORBIDDEN when the approving actor is the submitter (compare actor.user_id against the submitter recorded in the APPROVAL_STEP audit trail / a submitted_by column). Assumption: adding a nullable chain-snapshot column is acceptable; if schema change must be avoided, the per-step submitter-identity check alone closes the self-approval path.

Business error codes introduced/used by the new workflow endpoints (422 RECORD_APPROVAL_MATRIX_NOT_BOUND / RECORD_MODULE_UNKNOWN, 403 APPROVAL_SELF_REVIEW_FORBIDDEN / APPROVAL_ROLE_MISMATCH, 409 SIGN_STEP_OUT_OF_ORDER / RECORD_INVALID_TRANSITION) are not declared via responses= in OpenAPI, so they exist only in source. This is family-consistent (only the calc-module endpoints use responses=) and the frontend parses the {code, message, detail, trace_id} envelope generically via src/api/errors.ts, so no consumer breakage — but contract consumers cannot discover these codes from the baseline.

residual_risks: p9_013's _CREATE_BINDINGS INSERT has never inserted an actual row on any real database: dev pcs has 0 projects, pcs_test has 0 projects, and CI upgrades a fresh empty schema — the backfill's row-producing path (CROSS JOIN over existing projects) will run for the first time on the first project-bearing database this migration meets. SQL shape is standard correlated NOT EXISTS and was syntax-validated on PG18 by the dev/pcs_test upgrades, but the semantics on populated data are unexercised.

Consistent with the lossy label and pre-T1 rollback semantics, but operators should know a downgrade unbinds post-upgrade-created projects too.

pcs-backend/docs/schema_compact_orm.md:73 still lists deliverables.parent_deliverable_id after the p9_012 drop. The doc was last regenerated in the P2 era (commit c051754) and is broadly stale, so this is one symptom of pre-existing doc drift rather than an omission introduced by this batch.
testing_gaps: tests/alembic/test_p9_013_bind_default_record_matrix.py never executes the migration against any engine — it imports the module and asserts the rendered SQL strings (honestly documented in its docstring). The double-bind guard (projects that already have a RECORD binding must be skipped) is only string-asserted ('NOT EXISTS' in SQL); no test exercises the scenario with populated tables — e.g. an upgrade-time database with mixed bound/unbound projects — where a wrong predicate would either violate uq_project_signature_matrix_bindings_project_module or silently rebind projects.

findings.title: Two simultaneous signers: one signature silently erased
findings.suggested_fix: In `DeliverableService.sign_step`, load the version row with a row lock before any validation that derives from mutable state: replace `await db.get(DeliverableVersion, version_id)` with `select(DeliverableVersion).where(...).with_for_update()` (same pattern as the numbering path at deliverable_service.py:706), so the second concurrent signer blocks until the first commits and then fails `_assert_step_order` with 409. Add a two-session test (two async clients signing the same step concurrently) asserting exactly one 200 and one 409 and one signature entry. Assumption: serializing on the version row is acceptable; a jsonb array_append upsert would also work but changes the audit shape.

findings.title: Duplicate project_no POST returns 500, not 409
findings.suggested_fix: In `create_project`, wrap `db.flush()` (or the commit) in `try/except IntegrityError: await db.rollback(); raise PcsError(code="PROJECT_NO_CONFLICT", message=f"项目编号 {payload.project_no} 已存在", status=409)` — mirroring the WorkspaceNotFoundError branch five lines up. Add a test: two POSTs with the same project_no → second is 409.

findings.title: Project in PERSONAL workspace: success notice, dead signing
findings.suggested_fix: Default: enforce at the backend — after `db.get(Workspace, ...)`, `if workspace.workspace_type != 'FORMAL': raise PcsError(code='WORKSPACE_NOT_FORMAL', status=422, ...)` matching the gate the rest of the signing flow already applies (_guard.py). Also make the frontend match its own comment: filter `listWorkspaces` results to `workspace_type === 'FORMAL'` in ProjectAdminPage.tsx. Assumption: FORMAL is the only valid type for projects; if TEMPORARY should also be allowed, adjust the check accordingly.

findings.title: First-project race: default-matrix insert 500s without fallback
findings.suggested_fix: Copy the `_ensure_binding` pattern into `_get_or_create_default_record_matrix`: wrap the `db.add(matrix); await db.flush()` in try/except IntegrityError, `await db.rollback()` is NOT safe here (caller's project INSERT would be lost) — instead use a nested-transaction savepoint (`async with db.begin_nested():`) around the insert, then re-SELECT the matrix by (name, ACTIVE) and return the existing row. Add a test with two concurrent create_project calls against an empty signature_matrices table asserting both succeed.

findings.title: Pagination silently applies the un-applied audit filter
findings.suggested_fix: Move the freeze out of the load path: only the 查询 handler sets `appliedFilter` (and resets page to 1); make `loadAuditLogs` query with `appliedFilter` instead of `auditFilter`, and have the effect depend on `appliedFilter`. Then page changes can never pull un-applied inputs. Add a test: type a new filter, click page 2, assert the request still carries the previously applied action.

findings.title: Empty steps_json matrix turns submit-approval into 500
findings.suggested_fix: In `submit_approval`, right after `steps = SignatureMatrixService.parse_steps(matrix)`, add `if not steps: raise PcsError(code="SIGNATURE_MATRIX_INVALID", message=f"矩阵 {matrix.matrix_name!r} 没有可用步骤", status=422)` — the same loud-failure philosophy the parse_steps docstring already commits to. Test: bind a matrix with steps_json=[] and POST submit-approval → 422.

residual_risks: approval-step / submit-approval under concurrent double-submit converge on the scalar columns but write duplicate APPROVAL_STEP_PASSED / RECORD_TRANSITION audit rows (no row lock); lesser sibling of the sign_step lost-update finding — audit trail shows two approvals for one step advance.

e2e specs (pcs-frontend/e2e/deliverable_sign.spec.ts, record_actions.spec.ts, audit_log.spec.ts) were not adversarially reviewed this run (budget); mock approval-step is fully static (always step 2 of 2, never CHECKED), so no e2e exercises the terminal state of the record approval chain.

Mock sign-step enforces order but not sign_role / can_self_check / can_skip, although its header claims 语义照抄后端 — the 403 role-mismatch and 409 skip-forbidden branches cannot be reproduced in dev, so the dialog's disable-gates are the only defense ever exercised.

Audit export loop verified safe against the persona's partial-file scenario: downloadCsv runs only after the loop completes, so a page-26 failure yields an error alert and no file; a session-over 401 mid-loop still redirects via the (now code-gated) interceptor, which is intended.
testing_gaps: No concurrency test anywhere in test_deliverable_sign_step.py (30 tests) or test_record_approval_chain.py (9 tests) for two simultaneous signers/approvers — the lost-update and duplicate-audit classes are unguarded by CI.

handlers.test.ts '新端点的 handler 都注册了' ratchet lists only 9 of the ~17 signFlow endpoints (record write-actions ×6, submit-approval, approval-step, version snapshot, admin disable, POST /projects are absent), and for issue/sign-step/proxy it Ajv-validates test-authored literals rather than actual handler output — a response-shape drift in those handlers keeps the suite green (partially mitigated by signFlow.test.ts, which hits handlers but only asserts status/state fields).

Mock submit-approval returns approval_depth 2 / approval_role CHECKER while the backend default RECORD matrix is depth 3 (CHECKER→REVIEWER→APPROVER) — dev UI shows 'Step 1/2' against a system that will really run 3; no test pins the mock depth to SignatureMatrixService.DEFAULT_RECORD_STEPS.

The state-machine seed guard chain is sound (backend get_state_machine == seed JSON == served by mock via meta.ts:19/115), but nothing pins the meta handler's served shape beyond seed equality — if handlers.ts:992 ever serializes through a different transform, the pytest guard stays green.
